Temporary Bypass System Contingency Plan
Project: Construction of the Baseline Road Storm Drain Project — Job No. 1881
Location: Baseline Road (Tamarind Ave. to Cactus Ave.), City of Rialto, CA 92376
Date: March 16, 2026
Purpose
This document provides the procedures, equipment, and controls for deploying a contingency sewer bypass plan if needed due to an unplanned disruption, leak, or failure with the temporary sewer bypass system. This plan is submitted to satisfy the requirement in the RFI‑003 response.
---
Activation Criteria
Flow is obstructed and normal gravity service cannot be maintained.
A leak, break, or failure is observed in the active work area.
Infiltration/surcharge prevents safe operations.
The City or Construction Management directs activation.
> Once activated, operate continuously until gravity service is safely restored.
---
References
Plan reference: Bypass suction and discharge manholes are the existing upstream and downstream sanitary sewer manholes shown on Sheet 12 (Line D) of the project plans. (Exact manhole IDs to be verified in the field; see sheet callouts and detail.)
Contacts, spill vendors, and standard procedures: Consistent with C.P. Construction’s prior Sewer Bypass Plan (retained where applicable).
---
Roles & Responsibilities
C.P. Construction (Contractor): Deploys, operates, monitors, and demobilizes the bypass; maintains continuous service; prevents spills; documents activities.
Construction Management (Fountainhead) – Coordination Contact: Richard Hennings, Assistant Resident Engineer, Direct: (626) 641‑8013. (Coordination only.)
Emergency Vendors: Houston Harris Co. for vacuum/pumping support; West Coast Sanitation as backup.
---
Bypass System Configuration (Emergency Use)
Locations
Suction: Existing upstream sanitary sewer manhole per Sheet 12.
Discharge: Existing downstream sanitary sewer manhole per Sheet 12.
(Exact field ties per staking and inspector direction.)
Pumps (with redundancy)
Two (2) 4‑inch diesel chopper pumps (lead & standby)
Two (2) 6‑inch diesel chopper pumps (lead & standby)
Performance, TDH, and curves per manufacturer specs (see Attachment B).
Hoses & Fittings
Suction hoses with appropriate strainers
Discharge hoses sized to maintain design flow with minimal headloss
Required couplings, restraints, check valves, and plugs
Sandbags/cribbing to secure crossings and prevent movement
Bypass Layout Drawing
Attachment A (to be provided) will show emergency hose routing from upstream to downstream manhole, including all crossings, protection, and traffic control notes.
---
Pre‑Activation Checks (Field)
Verify suction/discharge manhole access and condition (gas test, ventilation).
Confirm pump readiness, fuel, and safe placement outside excavation limits.
Stage spill kits, sandbags, and vacuum truck contact information.
Hydrostatic test all discharge hoses/lines prior to live use; verify no leaks.
---
Activation & Operation Procedure
Install suction/discharge hoses per Attachment A; secure with sandbags/anchors.
Set and secure pumps on level ground; deploy secondary containment (see Section 10).
Prime/start the primary pump; bring discharge up gradually; verify downstream acceptance.
Start standby pump(s) as automatic backup with lead‑lag controls or manual hot standby.
Continuously monitor pump operation, hose integrity, and flow.
Daily shut‑down (if directed): Flush, secure pumps/hoses, maintain site control.
Demobilize only after inspector authorizes return to gravity service.
---
Monitoring & Documentation
Maintain a Bypass Log (times, pump hours, inspections, issues, corrective actions).
Photo‑document any leaks/spills, containment, cleanup, and restoration.
Keep copies of hydrostatic test, inspection checklists, and vendor callouts on file.
---
Spill Prevention & Response
Prevention: Double‑check all joints and restraints; protect inlets; maintain standby capacity at all times.
If spill occurs: Stop/contain at source; deploy absorbents/berms; prevent entry to storm drains; notify contacts; call Houston Harris Co. for vacuum recovery; West Coast Sanitation as backup.
Decon/Disposal: Pressure wash impacted areas; capture wash water; return to sanitary system; dispose per regulations.
---
Pump Protection & Secondary Containment
Establish a contained area around pumps consisting of double sandbag berms lined with visqueen to capture any drips/overflows and protect from storm runoff. (See Attachment C – Pump Protection Plan.)
---
Safety & Site Controls
Traffic Control: Delineate hose crossings; use plates or ramps where required; maintain access.
Confined Space: Manhole entry by trained personnel only; follow permit‑required procedures.
Air Monitoring: Test before entry; follow ventilation requirements.
Fuel Management: Store diesel and refuel away from drains with spill kits on hand.
Noise/Lighting: Use sound‑attenuated units; provide lighting for evening operations if needed.
---
Demobilization & Restoration
Cease pumping; flush discharge; remove hoses and plugs; restore manholes to normal.
Remove sandbags/visqueen; collect and dispose of any contaminated materials.
Restore surface, traffic control, and site to pre‑existing condition.
File final Bypass Log and any incident documentation.
